title: firstChild
body:
`node.firstChild` is the first child node of any kind, and in real markup that is nearly always a whitespace [[Text Node]] rather than the element you wanted. ```html
text

hello

``` ```js const d = document.querySelector("#d"); d.firstChild; // the text node " text\n\t", not the

d.firstElementChild; // the

``` This is one of the reasons the legacy `getElementById` / `getElementsByTagName` trio was painful to walk a tree with, and part of why `querySelector` arrived in 2012. Use `firstElementChild`, `children`, or just a selector, and reserve `firstChild` /`childNodes` for when you genuinely want the text too. See [[Selecting Nodes]] and [[Element Node]].
